stem.en: A larva feeds for some time before it changes into an adult. A lizard hatches with no larva stage. What does this difference show?

text.en: Larvae always grow much faster than young lizards

feedback.en: The difference here is not about speed of growth.

text.en: A larva feeds at a much later stage than a lizard does

feedback.en: Both animals feed after hatching. The larva stage is what differs.

text.en: A lizard egg contains no yolk at all

feedback.en: A lizard egg has a lot of yolk. That is why no larva stage is needed.

text.en: A lizard egg stores enough food for hatching

feedback.en: Yes. A larva must feed to reach the stage that a lizard egg already reaches.

explanation.en: A lizard egg holds enough yolk to nourish the embryo until it hatches into a young one. An egg with less yolk produces a larva, which gets its food by feeding after hatching.

hints.en: Where does the food come from before hatching?
What is the larva stage for?
